about: Which CI job proves which live engine, and the only skips each job may report.
Read by scripts/check_live_skips.py (fails a job on an unexpected skip) and by
services/connector_ci_evidence.py (an engine is live-verified only when a job
listed here ran it green). Every expected_skips entry needs `test` (fnmatch on the
pytest node id), `reason` (regex the skip message must match) and `why`.
Modes: strict = every skip must be expected; engine_scoped = a skip whose message
names one of the job's engines must be expected (whole-suite jobs), even when it also
names an engine the job lacks (mariadb counts as mysql, pg-wire as postgresql);
report = counted and published, never fails the job.
Genuine two-engine skips are allowlisted one by one; `only_jobs` limits an entry to
the jobs where the partner engine is absent (e.g. SQL Server in api-tests).
`proves` names the engines the job is the proof for; the others in `engines` are
peers it needs. An engine is live-verified only by a green job that proves it, and a
red job that proves it makes it red. `emulated` engines ran against an emulator.
run green before the job counts, e.g. both SQL Server drivers.

engine-suite.report_engines_why: Kafka and SQL Server cannot run on the development machine, so their nightly skips could not be proven absent before this landed. They are counted per engine and published (evidence never calls them live-verified while any skip names them) but do not fail the nightly. Move them to enforced once a nightly shows zero; cdc-sqlserver already enforces SQL Server on every PR.

api-tests.report_engines_why: The universal-matrix cells with a BigQuery / GCS / ADLS emulator *source* (8 each) skip as 'not reachable' with the emulators running; not yet investigated. Counted and published, never live-verified, not failing the shard.
api-tests.measurement: 2026-11-13: the ~3,330 api-tests skips replayed under the shards' exact environment: 284 named a PostgreSQL / MySQL / Mongo / Redis / emulator engine the job starts, the rest (~2,820) are external (SaaS templates, Oracle, SQL Server, Kafka, Iceberg, vector stores, MinIO, MariaDB, real clouds). With .github/ci-live-engines.vars, 104 of the 284 ran and passed locally; see the PR for the rest.

expected_skips.why: Needs a second PostgreSQL running wal_level=replica; the CI PostgreSQL runs wal_level=logical for every CDC test.

Needs a PostgreSQL without logical decoding; the CI PostgreSQL has it on for CDC.
Changes server-wide MySQL settings (SET GLOBAL); needs a dedicated MySQL, not the one every other test in the shard shares.
Needs a TLS-configured MySQL and its CA file; the CI MySQL is plaintext.
Needs a second MySQL account without REPLICATION grants; CI has only the dataflow account, which holds them for CDC.
By design: this Postgres-only file skips its MySQL leg whenever MySQL is up; the MySQL CDC e2e covers it.
By design: this Postgres-only file skips its MySQL leg whenever MySQL is up; the MySQL sandbox covers it.
